title: Korea Stock Market Today, Oct 26, 2026: KOSPI -1.46%, KOSDAQ -3.26% as Lunit Hits Limit-Up
content:
KOSPI closed at 5,469.47, down 1.46%, and KOSDAQ closed at 727.21, down 3.26%, as KOSDAQ fell more than KOSPI and sentiment toward small and mid-cap growth stocks weakened. Individual themes still diverged: Lunit's cancer drug research tie-up with U.S. biotech Summit Therapeutics, Robotis' actuator supply deal for the Microduck robot, Bigwave Robotics and rotation into newly listed stocks, and Contec's continued gains on its space optical communication results.

1. KOSPI and KOSDAQ fall together — themes diverge

KOSPI fell 80.83 points (-1.46%) to 5,469.47 and KOSDAQ fell 24.48 points (-3.26%) to 727.21. KOSDAQ's larger drop pointed to weaker sentiment toward small and mid-cap growth stocks.

2. Lunit teams up with Summit Therapeutics on cancer drug research — medical AI stocks strengthen

Medical AI company Lunit hit its daily upper limit on news that it will join U.S. biotech Summit Therapeutics in AI biomarker research for the next-generation immuno-oncology drug ivonescimab. Lunit plans to use its AI pathology platform, Lunit SCOPE IO, to analyze tumor tissue and select patients likely to respond. Summit has drawn a $2 billion strategic investment from AstraZeneca and is pushing cancer drug development, and the use of Lunit's AI in global drug development stirred investor sentiment. Names in focus included Lunit, Vuno, 3Billion, Lemonhealthcare, Neurophet, Syntekabio, OncoCross and Selvas Healthcare. Interest also spread to AI broadly, including SKAI, AgentAI, Crowdworks and Polaris AI. The Lunit deal does not mean direct joint research or supply contracts for the other companies, and some moves reflect theme buying on AI industry growth expectations.

3. Robotis signs an actuator supply deal for Microduck — robot parts stocks in focus

Robot company Robotis drew attention for signing a supply contract with France's Pollen Robotics for actuators used in its small bipedal robot, Microduck. The initial requested volume is 750,000 actuators, enough for 50,000 robots, and Pollen Robotics expects next year's actuator demand could exceed 1 million. Each Microduck carries 15 actuators. Expectations for a bigger supply of actuators, the core parts that move a robot's joints, lifted Robotis, Korea PIM, Wonik Holdings, Samhyun, Everybot, T Robotics, Anrobotics, SPG and Halla Casting.

4. Bigwave Robotics hits its upper limit — rotation into newly listed robot stocks

Newly listed robot company Bigwave Robotics rose strongly, and buying spread across newly listed robot stocks. Expectations for industrial robot automation and the physical AI market continued, with the supply and demand effect typical of early-listing stocks added on top. Names in focus included Bigwave Robotics, Haechitec, Brils and Alt. For new listings, tradable share supply, trading value and early order flow can move the price as much as earnings and business strength.

5. Rotation among new listings — interest spreads to bio, robot and AI names

As rotation among early-listing stocks continued, MS Bio, Ingenia Therapeutics, Remedi, Melcon and Neosapience were also mentioned. Buying moved across different sectors, including bio, medical devices, AI and robots. Not every stock rose on the same news, so each company's listing background, business, same-day disclosures and trading flow should be separated.

6. Contec extends gains on its space optical communication results — space stocks in focus

Space ground station company Contec kept rising after succeeding in Korea's first optical communication data reception test with a low-earth-orbit satellite in actual operation, and after results from satellite data transmission and reception through its own ground station drew attention. High-speed optical communication can move large amounts of data faster than existing radio-frequency links, which stirred expectations for expanded space communication infrastructure. Contec, AP Satellite and LK Samyang were in focus.
